4º de Primaria · Inglés · Tema 9

Present continuous

Nombre: ______________________   Fecha: ___________

Qué vas a aprender

  • Talk about actions happening now (lo que está pasando ahora)
  • Form the present continuous with am, is, are + -ing
  • Spell the -ing form correctly
  • Ask «What are you doing?» and describe a picture
  • Choose between the present simple and the present continuous
  • Give short answers: Yes, I am / No, he isn't
  • Describe where things are in a picture
  • Talk about the weather and clothes now and have a phone conversation

Para pensar

Tu madre te llama por teléfono y te pregunta «What are you doing?». ¿Qué te está preguntando y cómo le contestarías?

Explicación

1. Actions happening now

We use the present continuous for actions that are happening now, at this moment: «Look! It's raining», «Shh! The baby is sleeping», «I'm reading a great book».

It's different from the present simple, which is for habits: «I read every night» (costumbre) / «I'm reading now» (ahora). En castellano: es igual que «estoy leyendo», «está lloviendo». La terminación -ing equivale a nuestro -ando o -iendo: reading = leyendo, playing = jugando.

2. How to make it: be + -ing

The present continuous has two parts: the verb to be (am, is, are) + the main verb with -ing. «I am playing», «She is eating», «They are running».

We use am with I; is with he, she, it; and are with you, we, they. In conversation we use short forms: I'm, she's, they're. En castellano: to be hace el papel de «estar»: «I'm eating» = «estoy comiendo».

3. Spelling the -ing form

Most verbs just add -ing: read → reading, play → playing, cook → cooking. Verbs ending in -e lose the e: write → writing, dance → dancing, make → making.

Short verbs with consonant + vowel + consonant double the last letter: run → running, swim → swimming, sit → sitting, get → getting. Truco: si la palabra es corta y termina en consonante-vocal-consonante, ¡dobla la última letra!

4. Present simple or present continuous?

We have two presents in English, and they are used for different things:

  • The present simple is for habits and things that are always true: «I play football every Saturday.» «Leo goes hiking every day.»
  • The present continuous is for things that are happening now, at this moment: «I am playing football now.» «Leo is sitting on a rock right now.»

Time words help you choose:

  • Present simple: every day, usually, always, never, on Mondays, at the weekend.
  • Present continuous: now, right now, at the moment, today, look!, listen!

Compare these pairs:

  • «My dad works in a bank.» (his job) / «Today my dad is working at home.» (only today)
  • «It rains a lot in Galicia.» (a fact) / «Look! It's raining!» (now)
  • «I usually wear jeans.» / «Today I'm wearing a dress.»

A useful trick: if you can add now or at the moment to the sentence, use the continuous. If you can add every day or usually, use the simple.

Some verbs are almost never in the continuous form: like, love, hate, want, know, have got. We say «I like this song» (not «I'm liking»), and «I know the answer» (not «I'm knowing»).

5. Negative: I'm not…

To make a negative, put not after am, is or are: «I'm not sleeping», «He isn't watching TV» (is not), «We aren't playing» (are not).

It's very useful to correct someone: «I'm not sleeping, I'm thinking!», «She isn't crying, she's laughing!». En castellano: «no estoy durmiendo» → «I'm not sleeping». Fíjate en que con I no existe la forma «amn't»: decimos siempre I'm not.

6. Questions: What are you doing?

For questions, put am, is, are first: «Are you listening?», «Is she sleeping?». Short answers: «Yes, I am. / No, I'm not.», «Yes, she is. / No, she isn't.»

The most famous question is What are you doing? (¿Qué estás haciendo?). Also: «Where are you going?», «Who is she talking to?». En castellano: aquí no necesitamos do: el verbo to be ya hace de ayudante.

7. Short answers

When somebody asks a yes / no question in the present continuous, we can answer with a short answer. We use the verb be, not the -ing verb:

  • «Are you watching TV?» → «Yes, I am.» / «No, I'm not.»
  • «Is she reading?» → «Yes, she is.» / «No, she isn't.»
  • «Is it raining?» → «Yes, it is.» / «No, it isn't.»
  • «Are they playing?» → «Yes, they are.» / «No, they aren't.»
  • «Are we winning?» → «Yes, we are!» / «No, we aren't.»

Important rules:

  • In affirmative short answers, we don't use contractions: «Yes, I am», not «Yes, I'm».
  • In negative short answers, we usually use contractions: «No, she isn't».
  • Don't repeat the -ing verb: «Yes, I am», not «Yes, I am watching».

After a short answer, you can add more information to keep the conversation going:

  • «Are you doing your homework?» → «No, I'm not. I'm drawing.»
  • «Is your brother sleeping?» → «Yes, he is. He's very tired.»

8. Time words: now, at the moment, look!

The present continuous often comes with now, right now, at the moment (en este momento) and today: «We're having lunch at the moment», «She's working at home today».

Also, when we want someone to see something, we say Look! or Listen!: «Look! The cat is climbing the tree!», «Listen! Someone is singing». Compare with the present simple time words: every day, usually, on Mondays. Pista: si ves now, piensa en -ing.

9. Describing a picture

The present continuous is perfect to describe a picture or a photo. Look at the park: «A boy is flying a kite. Two girls are skipping (saltando a la comba). A man is walking his dog. A baby is sleeping in a pram. The sun is shining».

Start with In the picture or I can see: «In the picture, I can see a family. They are having a picnic». Consejo: usa is con una persona y are con dos o más.

10. Where is it? Positions in a picture

To describe a picture, we need to say what people are doing and where they are. These expressions are very useful:

  • in the middle (en el centro): «In the middle, there is a big tree.»
  • on the left (a la izquierda) / on the right (a la derecha): «On the left, a girl is riding a bike.»
  • at the top (arriba) / at the bottom (abajo): «At the top, some birds are flying.»
  • in the background (al fondo): «In the background, there are mountains.»
  • in the foreground (en primer plano): «In the foreground, a dog is sleeping.»
  • next to (al lado de), behind (detrás de), in front of (delante de), under (debajo de).

Now read this description:

This is a picture of a park on a sunny day. In the middle, there is a fountain and two children are playing with water. On the left, a man is reading a newspaper on a bench. On the right, a woman is walking her dog. In the background, some boys are playing football. At the top, the sun is shining. Everybody is having a good time!

A good description goes in order: first say what the picture shows in general, then describe the middle, then the left and the right, and finally the background. Don't jump from one place to another, or your listener will get lost!

Use there is / there are for things, and the present continuous for actions.

11. Reading: a postcard from the beach

Read Paula's postcard: «Dear Grandma, I'm writing from the beach in Menorca! It's sunny and hot. Right now Mum is reading a book under the umbrella and Dad is swimming. My little brother is building a sandcastle. He isn't wearing his hat, oops! I'm eating a delicious ice cream. Some children are playing volleyball near us. We're having a great time! Love, Paula.»

Answer: What is Dad doing? Is her brother wearing his hat? What is Paula eating?

12. Let's practise: mime and guess

Play Mime and guess (mímica). One student picks a card with an action and mimes it in front of the class: brushing teeth, playing the piano, riding a horse, eating spaghetti… The class asks: «Are you swimming?» – «No, I'm not!» – «Are you dancing?» – «Yes, I am!».

Then the class says the full sentence: «She's dancing!». Consejo: fíjate en si preguntas a la persona («Are you…?») o hablas de ella al resto de la clase («She's… / He's…»).

13. Weather and clothes right now

The present continuous is perfect for talking about the weather and the clothes we are wearing now.

Weather now:

  • «It's raining.» (Está lloviendo.)
  • «It's snowing.» (Está nevando.)
  • «The sun is shining.» (Brilla el sol.)
  • «The wind is blowing.» (Sopla el viento.)

But with adjectives we use is: «It's sunny.» «It's windy.» «It's cold.» «It's cloudy.»

Clothes now:

  • «I'm wearing a blue T-shirt and jeans.»
  • «She's wearing a raincoat and boots, because it's raining.»
  • «They're wearing shorts and sandals, because it's hot.»
  • «What are you wearing today?»

Useful clothes words: jumper (jersey), coat (abrigo), raincoat (chubasquero), scarf (bufanda), gloves (guantes), cap (gorra), trainers (zapatillas de deporte), shorts (pantalones cortos).

Remember that we say wear for clothes, glasses and jewellery: «He's wearing glasses.»

Look out of the window now. What's the weather like? And what are you wearing? Tell your partner!

14. On the phone

When we talk on the phone or send a message, we often ask what the other person is doing now. Here are some useful phrases:

Starting the call:

  • «Hello! It's Leo.» (On the phone, we say It's…, not I am….)
  • «Hi, Leo! How are you?»
  • «Can I speak to Nico, please?»

Asking and answering:

  • «What are you doing?» → «I'm watching a film.»
  • «Where are you?» → «I'm at the beach.»
  • «Are you busy?» (¿Estás ocupado?) → «No, I'm not. I'm just relaxing.»
  • «Who are you with?» → «I'm with my cousins.»

Ending the call:

  • «I have to go now.» (Tengo que irme.)
  • «Talk to you later!» / «See you soon!»
  • «Bye!»

In messages, people often use short forms: What r u doing? But at school, always write the full words: What are you doing?

Role-play: with a partner, imagine you are in different places (a zoo, a football match, the beach…). Call each other and describe what is happening around you.

Present continuous

Ejercicios

  1. Write the -ing form: play, make, sit.

  2. Complete with am, is or are: «They ___ singing.»

  3. Complete: «Look! The dog ___ (run).»

  4. Make it negative: «I'm sleeping.»

  5. Make it negative: «We are watching TV.»

  6. Make a question: «You are listening.»

  7. Short answer (no): «Is your brother studying?»

  8. Present simple or continuous? «I ___ (read) now.»

  9. Translate: «¿Qué estás haciendo?»

  10. Describe what three people in your house are doing now.

  11. Complete: Look! It ___ (snow).

  12. Answer: Are you reading? (yes)

  13. What do you say first on the phone?

  14. Translate: a la izquierda.

  15. Complete: I'm ___ (wear) a jumper.

  16. Choose: She (works / is working) in a bank. Today she (works / is working) at home.

  17. Answer: Are they playing football? (no)

  18. Write two sentences about the weather now.

  19. Correct: I'm liking this song.

  20. Write what Leo's friends are doing in the reading.

  21. Describe a picture of a park with five positions.

  22. Write a phone conversation from a zoo.

  23. Write five sentences: what you usually do and what you are doing today.

  24. Describe what your classmates are wearing today.

Practica

  1. We use the present continuous for…

    1. A) habits
    2. B) the past
    3. C) actions happening now

  2. «I ___ reading.»

    1. A) am
    2. B) is
    3. C) are

  3. «They ___ playing.»

    1. A) is
    2. B) are
    3. C) am

  4. The -ing form of «swim» is…

    1. A) swiming
    2. B) swimming
    3. C) swimmng

  5. The -ing form of «write» is…

    1. A) writeing
    2. B) writting
    3. C) writing

  6. «He ___ watching TV.» (negativa)

    1. A) isn't
    2. B) doesn't
    3. C) aren't

  7. «___ you listening?»

    1. A) Do
    2. B) Is
    3. C) Are

  8. «What are you doing?» means…

    1. A) ¿Qué haces cada día?
    2. B) ¿Qué estás haciendo?
    3. C) ¿Qué hiciste?

  9. Which sentence is present continuous?

    1. A) She's dancing.
    2. B) She dances.
    3. C) She danced.

  10. Which word goes with the present continuous?

    1. A) at the moment
    2. B) every day
    3. C) usually

  11. I ___ my homework every day.

    1. A) am doing
    2. B) do
    3. C) doing

  12. Is she sleeping? Yes, she ___ .

    1. A) 's
    2. B) sleeping
    3. C) is

  13. «Al fondo» is…

    1. A) on the left
    2. B) in the background
    3. C) at the top

  14. It's ___ . Take your raincoat.

    1. A) raining
    2. B) rain
    3. C) rains

  15. On the phone we say…

    1. A) I am Leo.
    2. B) Here Leo.
    3. C) It's Leo.

Explícalo con tus palabras

Incluye: Para qué sirve el presente continuo; Cómo se forma con am, is, are y -ing; Las reglas de ortografía de -ing; Cómo se hacen negativas y preguntas, y en qué se diferencia del presente simple.

Soluciones

  1. C) Ahora.
  2. A) I + am.
  3. B) They + are.
  4. B) Doble m.
  5. C) Se quita la e.
  6. A) is not.
  7. C) you + are.
  8. B) Ahora mismo.
  9. A) is + -ing.
  10. A) En este momento.
  11. B) Simple or continuous.
  12. C) Short answers.
  13. B) Positions.
  14. A) Weather.
  15. C) Phone.
